newsitem.title: UK: Hardy in 2nd successful Indian oil well test.
newsitem.headline: Hardy in 2nd successful Indian oil well test.

text.p: Hardy Oil and Gas Plc, the independent exploration and production company, said on Tuesday that a second well in the PY-3 oilfield off the southeast coast of India is nearing completion.
The production well tested at a flow rate of 5,300 barrels per day (bpd) of 49 degrees API oil, the company said in a statement.
The company, which reported the successful completion of the first well in March, said two further wells will be drilled and the first production is expected in the second half of 1997.
PY-3 lies in block CY-OS-90/1 in the Cauvery basin.

Hardy said it recently acquired a 32.147 percent stake in block CB-OS/1 in the Cambay basin off northwest India from Vaalco Energy Inc, and will now act as operator. One discovery, thought potentially commercial, will be appraised later this year subject to rig availability.
Hardy also acquired from Vaalco a 25 percent interest in and operatorship of block CY-OS/2, adjacent to PY-3.
Separately, Hardy said it acquired a 30 percent stake and operatorship of block KG-OS-90/1, offshore east India in the Krishna Godavari basin.

"India is a territory which has recently become accessible for international exploration but shows signs of great potential and could become a new core area for Hardy," said chief executive John Walmsley in a statement.
The company also said that shareholders of Hindustan Oil Exploration Co (HOEC) approved at an EGM on April 4 Hardy's acquisition -- first announced in March -- of a 15.5 percent stake in HOEC.
